newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sells off Zellidja mining stake for $4.1 m.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sells off Zellidja mining stake for $4.1 m.

text.p: The Moroccan government has sold its 26 percent stake in the Zellidja lead mining firm for 39 million dirhams ($4.1 million), the privatisation ministry said on Tuesday.

The state-run Bureau de Recherches et Prospection Miniere (BRPM) ceded its 26 percent stake in Zellidja in favour of its shareholders, including ONA's subsidiary Compagnie Miniere de Toussit (CIT), the ministry said in a statement.
Morocco's largest conglomerate, ONA Group, bought stakes in four mines, including CIT and silver mine of Imiter, for more than 400 million dirhams in 1996.
After an inconclusive public tender in May 1996 and months of negotiations, the authorities decided to directly cede the BRPM stake in Zellidja for 39 million dirhams, the statement added.
Established in 1945 in the northeastern region of Oujda, Zellidja has an output of 100,000 tonnes of lead per year and employs a staff of 500.
Zellidja's turnover was 516 million dirhams in 1996, the ministry said but gave no comparative figures for 1995.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Zellidja was lasted traded at 582 dirhams.
